newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Evening Standard - 10 April 1997.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Evening Standard - 10 April 1997.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
-- RUIN OF THE MAN WHO MISSED OUT ON 10M STG LOTTERY WIN

A Londoner was driven to run up huge gambling debts and commit fraud against his employers after 33 of his office colleagues won 10m stg between them on the National Lottery jackpot. The man, London housing official Tony George, passed up the opportunity to join their Lottery syndicate, and has now been sacked by Camden Council after confessing the fraud to police.
-- LANDMARK BOND PLAN FOR WELCOME BREAK

Investcorp is considering a landmark bond issue as a way of financing its 436m stg purchase of Granada's Welcome Break motorway service stations chain. The issue, which might raise as much as 350m stg, would be backed by the Welcome Break chain's cashflows and assets, and would be the first instance of such a structure being used to finance a management buy-out.
-- POUND PUTS ON A SHOW FOR KEN AND EDDIE

As the Chancellor Kenneth Clarke and Bank of England Governor Eddie George prepare for their last pre-election meeting, sterling has reached fresh highs against Continental currencies. Sterling advanced over the 9.4 franc line against the French currency, the first time this has happened since 1992 when Britain was forced to leave the exchange rate mechanism.

-- US PLAN FOR UK BROKERS TO INSURE CLIENTS' CASH US insurer Asset Guaranty is launching a campaign today to raise awareness among smaller British investors that they can insure their stocks and shares up to 5m stg to guard against their stockbrokers going bust. Currently, thousands of small investors are protected up to only 48,000 stg by the Investors Compensation Scheme, as an insurance against stockbroker collapse.
-- THIRD MAN QUITS EXCHANGE FOR NEW JOB DOWN UNDER

A third senior official at the Hong Kong Exchange has resigned, this time to take up a similar post at the Australian Stock Exchange. The departing official, Paul Phenix, who is largely credited with ridding the market of trading abuses in the last two years, is said to have been reluctant to bend to the will of new chief executive Alex Tsui.
South Korean prosecutors are to question politicians involved in the loans-for-favours scandal, after receiving a list of names from the jailed founder of the Hanbo Group, Chung Tae-soo.
